why: Inserting the new principle made the model prefer keeping very short (1–4 word) complements attached to their predicate, so cuts moved later and improved cohesion mainly for longer pieces and lists (largest gains in the ≤99/≤10/≤7 bins), but that same shift caused more harmful splits in short/medium contexts (some ≤3–≤7 pairs got worse). Removing Examples E7/E4/E8 removed counterexamples that would have constrained those bad short-context moves.
lesson: A later revision should respect that preserving 1–4-word predicate complements improves long-span cohesion but must keep examples (or guidance) that prevent creating subject–verb or other harmful short-context splits.
blamed: Insert concise core principle (keep short 1–4 word complements with predicate)
